label: pseudoparaphyllium
parent: is_a PO_0005679 (portion of plant epidermis); part_of PO_0030020 (gametophore axis)
definition: A portion of plant epidermis (PO:0005679) that is a filamentous, scale-like or leaf-like outgrowth of a gametophore axis (PO:0030020), found only around branch primordia of pleurocarpous mosses.
reason: In moss floras this is a separate structure from paraphyllium (PO_0030069): pseudoparaphyllia occur only around branch buds, while paraphyllia grow between the leaves along the stem. Mapping it to paraphyllium would be wrong. Propose it to PO (Bryophytes subset) next to paraphyllium.

'Pseudo' means it is not a true rhizome. The warty organ that is brown outside and red inside is probably the tuber-like body of a root parasite, so mapping it to rhizome (PO_0004542) is doubtful. The examples do not settle which organ it is.

Two different senses. 'Tentacules glanduligères' are Drosera's stalked glands, which are emergences rather than plain glandular trichomes (PO_0004509). 'Up to 8 inconspicuous tentacles' are appendages of some other organ. No single class fits.
Narrower: the first leaves of a seedling, given with their own leaflet pairs, are juvenile leaves distinct from adult ones. The leaflet-pair counts then use the count-of-parts pattern on this bearer.
Fragment of French '-sérié(es)' ('3-sérié', '10-13-sériées'), meaning arranged in n series. That is a quality word; the previous review rejected 'seriate' as not a structure.
Narrower: a flat, flush gland on the leaf. It follows rule C265 (gland -> portion of secretory tissue).
French 'axe floral' means either the inflorescence axis (PO_0020122) or the receptacle (PO_0009064). Hooked, rusty and velvety axes suggest the first, but this cannot be decided without the taxon.
Fragment of French '-jugué(es)' (= -jugate, pairs of leaflets). It belongs in the counted-parts rule 'jugate -> leaflet, collection size 2'; add the French form 'jugué' there.
A general part ('languette', 'produced into a triangular tongue') that needs the organ it belongs to, like 'appendage' and 'lobule' in the previous review.
'Appendage' was rejected as a general part that needs its organ. 'Primary' only gives a rank in a series, and the organ is not stated.
Same as 'primary appendage': a general part with a rank, and no organ.

label: false indusium
parent: is_a PO_0025001 (cardinal organ part); part_of PO_0009025 (vascular leaf)
definition: A cardinal organ part (PO:0025001) that is a reflexed and usually modified, often membranous portion of the leaf margin (PO:0020128) of a fertile vascular leaf (PO:0009025), covering the marginal sori (PO:0025359), as in Pteridaceae.
reason: Common in fern floras. It is not an indusium (FLOPO_0986020, an outgrowth from the leaf surface) but the folded leaf margin itself. Propose it to PO together with indusium.
Narrower: 'inner' is a position in the corona's series. This follows the precedent C373/C374 (inner/outer tepal -> tepal).
The tip of an existing FLOPO class, expressed with the region reading apex (as in context word 'at the tip').
Bad singular of 'coccus'. A coccus is one carpel unit of a schizocarpic capsule (Euphorbiaceae), so it is narrower than mericarp, the carpel unit of a schizocarp.
A row is an arrangement of glands, not a structure. The bearer is gland (PO_0005656), and the number of rows describes how the glands are arranged.
A 'per X' container phrase of a count, like 'per node' and 'per axil' in the previous review.

label: style head
parent: is_a PO_0025001 (cardinal organ part); part_of PO_0009074 (style)
definition: A cardinal organ part (PO:0025001) that is the enlarged, often pentagonal, ovoid or globose distal portion of a style (PO:0009074), bearing the stigmatic surfaces and in Apocynaceae secreting the adhesive that attaches the pollinia or translators.
reason: A standard structure in Apocynaceae and Convolvulaceae descriptions with its own shapes (globose, deltoid, ovoid). It is not just the style apex. PO has style and stigma only. Propose it to PO, built like stylopodium (FLOPO_0986022).
'2n = 28' is a chromosome number, a quality of the plant ('chromosome' was rejected as not a structure).
Exact for the Malvaceae use (FNA): the involucel of Hibiscus and its relatives is the epicalyx, and its stellate-tomentose bractlets, 8-10 of them, are epicalyx segments.
The 'lips' are the rim of a cup-shaped involucre (dark-edged, revolute), so they are the margin of the involucre. Confidence is low because the family is not known.
Unclear structure: an aril-like rim, a hilar ring or something specific to one family. It cannot be grounded without the taxon.
'1-2-serrate' gives how many times the margin is serrate (simply or doubly). It is a quality word, not a part.

PO has no general spine class, only spines by origin (spine leaf PO_0025173, spine stipule PO_0025174, spine petiole PO_0025613). The colours suggest cacti (leaf spines), but the origin is not stated, and 'tip' alone was rejected as general.
Second term of a ratio to another part ('lengths 1-1.3 times corollas'), pattern 10.
Ratio of two dimensions of the same bearer ('height 0.5-1 times diam.'), pattern 11.
The perianth at the fruiting stage. The context word 'fruiting' already reads as stage PO_0001002, so there is no need for a new class.
'Embryo with 1 full spiral' gives how far the embryo is coiled, a shape quality of the embryo (PO_0009009).
PO lists hypogynium as a synonym of gynophore, so the lobes are lobes of that class. Note that in Scleria the hypogynium is a disc under the nut, so PO's synonym is loose.
'Leaves in pseudowhorls of 5' is an arrangement (leaves crowded so they look whorled), a quality of the leaves rather than a structure.
